model.display_name: VibeVoice-ASR-Streaming-1.5B (streaming speech-to-text LLM, one 3.47 s audio window per turn)
model.architecture: VibeVoice-ASR-Streaming: σ-VAE acoustic encoder + semantic encoder (SEANet/ConvNeXt-1d, 24 kHz -> 7.5 Hz latents) -> projector -> dense Qwen2.5-1.5B-shaped LM trained on 22-frame chunks + 4-frame look-ahead; LiteRT-LM generic audio path as a multi-turn conversation (raw-waveform frames, no mel)

variants.quantization: LM: int4 blockwise-128 min-max, int8 embedding; audio encoder: int8 dynamic on linears, fp32 convs, 3.47 s (26-frame) window

recommended.reason: LM on Metal: 1766 tok/s prefill / 114 tok/s decode vs 305 / 56 on CPU; 0.33 s per 2.93 s chunk end-to-end; the audio encoder stays on CPU (audio_backend cpu)
Galaxy S26: LM on OpenCL 628 tok/s prefill / 46.3 tok/s decode vs 317 / 46.5 on CPU, peak 1483 MB vs 2511 MB; the audio encoder must stay on CPU (audio_backend cpu)

platform_notes: Drive it as a MULTI-TURN conversation: one user turn = one audio window of 83 200 samples at 24 kHz (26 frames x 3200), then advance 70 400 samples (22 frames) keeping the 4-frame look-ahead; zero-pad the last window. Fed a whole clip in one turn the model transcribes only the last 3.5 s

Bare-prompt template (no ChatML): the vendor's streaming prompt is rendered once; each model turn ends with <|text_chunk_end|>; stop tokens <|text_chunk_end|> / <|endoftext|>. Hotwords: a system message '... with these keys: speaker, content and extra info: <words>'
audio_backend must be cpu (--audio_backend=cpu / audio_backend=CPU()); the LM may run on gpu

Accuracy: 20 LibriSpeech dev-clean clips (448 words, 73 windows), WER after stripping the 'Speaker N:' label: 7.81 % macOS CPU, 6.92 % LM-on-Metal, 7.81 % Galaxy S26 CPU, 7.14 % Galaxy S26 LM-on-GPU (fp32 PyTorch reference of the vendor streaming protocol 7.59 %; the non-streaming VibeVoice-ASR-BitNet bundle scores 2.68 % on the same clips with a 30 s window)
KV budget 2048 tokens ~ 2.5 minutes of continuous audio per conversation (about 40 tokens per 2.93 s chunk)
Peak private footprint on Galaxy S26 (streaming run, --report_peak_memory_footprint): 2511 MB CPU/CPU, 1483 MB LM-on-GPU; Pixel 8a: 2210 MB CPU/CPU, 2521 MB LM-on-Mali-GPU
Pixel 8a (Tensor G3): WER 7.81 % CPU, 7.37 % LM-on-Mali-GPU; keep the LM on the CPU there (Mali decode 12.7 tok/s vs 22.5 on CPU)

known_issues: Audio encoder does not run on the GPU delegates (Metal/WebGPU and Adreno OpenCL return an empty transcript, also with fp32 activations); keep audio_backend=cpu

Single-turn use (whole clip in one message, e.g. a chat app's audio attachment) yields only the last 3.5 s of transcript — the model was trained on the per-chunk protocol and needs the multi-turn loop
